study_design: Cross-national ecological correlation study using country-level milk consumption and cancer incidence rates
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Data on milk consumption for 9 time periods (1964-1994) and incidence rates of prostate, female breast, colon, and rectal cancers, mostly around 1993-1997, in 38 countries were obtained from the Food and Agriculture Organization and World Health Organization, respectively.
reason: The study evaluates country-level incidence rates of prostate cancer but does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Milk consumption was strongly correlated with incidence rates of prostate cancer (r = 0.65-0.69; all P < 0.0001) and breast cancer (r = 0.64-0.74; all P < 0.0001) in all the nine time periods examined.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row concerns country-level milk consumption and overall prostate cancer incidence rates, with no aggressive subtype specified.
